Extrapolation of ridge precision estimates across penalties

Source: R/ridgegraph.R
extrapolated_ridge.Rd

Combines ridge estimates at two effective penalties \(\kappa_1\) and \(\kappa_2 = r \kappa_1\) with weights \(\kappa_2 / (\kappa_2 - \kappa_1)\) and \(-\kappa_1 / (\kappa_2 - \kappa_1)\), after rescaling each estimate by its estimated scale. The population version of this combination differs from the precision matrix by a term of second order in the penalties.

Usage

extrapolated_ridge(x, lambda, ratio = 2)

Arguments

x

numeric data matrix with observations in rows.

lambda

first (smaller) penalty.

ratio

ratio \(\kappa_2 / \kappa_1 > 1\) of the effective penalties.

Value

A list with the combined matrix precision, its partial correlations pcor, the two penalties lambda, the two estimated effective penalties kappa and the weights.

Details

The sum of the absolute weights is \((r + 1) / (r - 1)\), which multiplies the sampling variability.

References

Arashi, M. and Ebrahim, E. K. (2026). What does a ridge network estimate? Effective penalty and leakage in ridge precision matrix estimation. Submitted.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rnorm(50 * 20), 50, 20)
fit <- extrapolated_ridge(x, lambda = 0.5)
fit$kappa
#> [1] 0.6662174 1.3324349
